_enforcement_note: Inventory + attestation only. Nothing gates execution on trust_tier here yet beyond router/select-adapter.js's own stub logic (ORCH-2), which only ever routes to trust_tier:trusted-local adapters.
_evidence_states_legend: verified = actually executed locally this session or a prior cited session, with a concrete command/artifact reference | claimed = documented by a first-party source (--help output, official docs, config file) but not exercised | unverified = plausible, genuinely no evidence either way | unsupported = adapter's own documentation/behavior explicitly rules this out | unavailable = the capability's prerequisite (e.g. a plugin) is not installed/reachable
_trust_tier_legend: untested (registered, zero executions of any kind) -> quarantined (some real executions, not yet enough to trust for unattended use) -> trusted-local (real track record, safe for local unattended use within HarnessKit's existing approval boundaries). Transitions only move forward one step at a time; a validator (scripts/validate-adapter-registry.js) rejects a record that skips untested -> trusted-local directly.
_trust_tier_transition_rule: untested -> quarantined -> trusted-local only. No adapter may be recorded as trusted-local without having first been quarantined in a prior revision of this file (enforced by scripts/validate-adapter-registry.js's --check-transition mode against git history; see R2 tests).

Plus a 4th real live call (2026-07-10, post-ENOENT-fix): reviewReadOnly against a fresh off-by-one clamp() fixture in os.tmpdir(), 18.8s, correct VERDICT: REJECT -- the first successful call through codex-adapter.js's own runCodex() spawn path since it was written; every prior real call was via direct Bash-tool CLI invocation, not this module.
incidents: 2026-07-09: `codex exec review --uncommitted` (Codex's own native review subcommand) correctly found the known-answer bug but its prose output has no 'VERDICT:' token, so parseCodexVerdict returns ERROR on it — do not route that subcommand's output through parseCodexVerdict.

2026-07-09: on this Windows machine, `--sandbox read-only` sub-command spawns Codex itself attempts (git diff/ls/cat for its own investigation) fail with a Windows logon-session error (CreateProcessAsUserW 1312); Codex still reached a correct verdict when the diff was supplied directly in the prompt (no exploration needed) — do not assume Codex's own investigative shell commands will succeed in this sandbox on this host.

2026-07-09: discovered loop-conductor.js#runWithTimeoutRetry uses execFileSync('codex', ...) without shell:true; on Windows this fails ENOENT (codex is an npm .cmd shim; Node's spawnSync/execFileSync do not apply PATHEXT resolution without shell:true) — confirmed by direct reproduction. This means every historical 'unexercised'/'spawn_failed' live_codex outcome on this machine was an environment bug, not (only) gating. A shell:true fix was attempted in loop-conductor.js and in this file's own runCodex(), both times correctly blocked by the Claude Code auto-mode safety classifier as introducing a cmd.exe argument-injection surface (args can include diff/prompt text). NEITHER file was modified after the block — loop-conductor.js is untouched (still has this bug, out of scope for the 2026-07-10 fix below), and scripts/codex-adapter.js's runCodex() used the bare (non-shell) spawnSync call and failed ENOENT on this machine until the fix below landed. The actual smoke-test evidence above was gathered via direct CLI invocation (Bash tool), which is not subject to this Node-specific spawn bug.

2026-07-10: FIXED in scripts/codex-adapter.js — no shell:true, no exec, no concatenated command strings. Root fix: on win32, resolve the real node_modules/.../codex.js the npm .cmd shim launches (read the shim's own generated wrapper text, or in the common case just check %APPDATA%\npm\codex.cmd directly) and invoke that resolved path via process.execPath, bypassing the shim/PATHEXT/shell question entirely. The untrusted prompt/diff text moved off argv entirely too (both platforms): codex exec's own documented stdin convention (`-` as the PROMPT argument) is used, prompt goes via spawnSync's `input` option. Verified three ways: (1) self-test unit-tests the shim-parsing regex against synthetic content, (2) self-test does a real (non-fixture) live resolution + `codex --version` spawn on this machine when codex is on PATH, (3) a full real reviewReadOnly() call against a fresh off-by-one fixture completed correctly end-to-end (see evidence_root) -- the first-ever successful call through this module's own runCodex(), not just via direct Bash-tool invocation. Also discovered along the way: `where codex`'s captured stdout is mis-decoded on this specific machine (non-ASCII/Hebrew Windows username -> OEM-codepage bytes read as UTF-8 -> mojibake path, ENOENT on the mis-decoded path) -- worked around by trying %APPDATA%\npm\codex.cmd first (process.env is always correctly decoded by Node, no codepage risk), falling back to `where` only for non-default npm global-prefix installs, where the mis-decoding risk is disclosed via a surfaced failure reason rather than a silent wrong guess. loop-conductor.js#runWithTimeoutRetry's separate execFileSync('codex', ...) call site still has the original bug -- not touched by this fix, named here so it isn't mistaken for fixed.
